previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of ileocolonic Crohn’s disease status post subtotal colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis, steroid-dependent and refractory to multiple biologics, was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and diarrhea consistent with a disease flare. He reported over 20 watery bowel movements in one night and increased abdominal pain, particularly in the left lower quadrant. Labs showed leukocytosis with a left shift, but stool studies were negative for C. diff, parasites, and CMV. He was treated with IV methylprednisone, transitioned to oral prednisone, and started on cholestyramine for diarrhea control. Pain was managed with Dilaudid and Tylenol, then switched to oral Percocet. His symptoms improved, diet was advanced, and he was discharged home on a temporary increased steroid dose with plans to follow up with gastroenterology for tapering and urology for kidney stone monitoring.
